record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How many k-abelian equivalence classes of words of a given length contain an nth power?

evidence.quote: How many k-abelian equivalence classes of words of a given length contain an nth power?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers k ≥ 1 and an alphabet Σ. For two finite words u, v ∈ Σ*, say that u and v are k-abelian equivalent, written u ∼_k v, if for every word w with |w| ≤ k the number of occurrences of w as a factor of u equals the number of occurrences of w as a factor of v. This is an equivalence relation on Σ*, and it preserves length. For an integer n ≥ 2, an n-th power is a word of the form w^n = ww···w (n copies of some word w ∈ Σ*).

Given integers k ≥ 1, n ≥ 2, an alphabet Σ, and a length N ≥ 1, determine the number of k-abelian equivalence classes of words in Σ^N that contain at least one n-th power; that is, compute (or give a closed-form / asymptotic expression for)
   f_{k,n,|Σ|}(N) := #{ [u]_{∼_k} : u ∈ Σ^N and there exists v ∈ [u]_{∼_k} such that v is an n-th power }.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on k-abelian equivalence (Karhumäki and collaborators) studies cardinalities of k-abelian equivalence classes and the existence of k-abelian n-th powers, but no source found provides a formula or asymptotic for the count of k-abelian classes of length-N words that contain an n-th power. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On cardinalities of k-abelian equivalence classes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the number of k-abelian equivalence classes of words of given length, giving polynomial growth results.
status_evidence.claim: Counts of k-abelian classes (without the n-th power restriction) are studied, but the restricted count is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses k-abelian n-th powers and repetition avoidance.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/avoidance of k-abelian powers is studied, but enumeration of equivalence classes containing them is not resolved.
